s: Who halted Harsha’s southward advance on the Narmada?
x: Pulakesin II defeated Harsha and stopped his southward march on the Narmada.
tq: Use the victor–event association to distinguish the Chalukya-Harsha conflict from the Pallava wars.
sec: Chalukya-Harsha conflict - victor, river, source, title

s:
The account of the conflict between Pulakesin II and Harsha is found in which of the following sources?
1. Aihole inscription composed by Ravikirti
2. Account of Hiuen Tsang
3. Kailasanatha temple inscription of Kanchi
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The Aihole inscription of Pulakesin II, composed by Ravikirti, and Hiuen Tsang’s account confirm the conflict. The Kailasanatha temple inscription is not the cited source for this event.
tq: Split the options by identifying the two sources directly associated with the event.
sec: Chalukya-Harsha conflict - victor, river, source, title

s: Pulakesin II assumed the title ‘Paramesvara’ after his conflict with Harsha. He was also styled as:
x: Pulakesin II was styled Dakshinapatheshwara, meaning lord of the south, in opposition to Harsha’s title Uttarapatheshwara.
tq: Discriminate between the similar directional titles of Pulakesin II and Harsha.
sec: Chalukya-Harsha conflict - victor, river, source, title

s: The conflict between Pulakesin II and Harsha is generally dated to:
x: The conflict is dated to 618 AD. It preceded the recording of the event in the Aihole inscription in 634 CE.
tq: Use the date options to separate the Harsha conflict from the later Pallava-Chalukya battles.
sec: Chalukya-Harsha conflict - victor, river, source, title

s:
Consider the following statements regarding women in Badami Chalukya administration:
1. Vijayabhattarika was the queen of Chandraditya.
2. Vijayabhattarika issued land grants in her own name.
3. Vijayabhattarika governed during the reign of Nandivarman II.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Vijayabhattarika, also known as Vijaya-mahadevi, was the queen of Chandraditya and governed while issuing land grants in her own name. She was not associated with the reign of Nandivarman II.
tq: Reject the statement that swaps a Chalukya queen’s context with a Pallava ruler.
sec: Women in administration - queens and princesses as governors

s: Which pair of queens commissioned the Virupaksha and Mallikarjuna temples at Pattadakal?
x: Lokamahadevi and Trailokyamahadevi, queens of Vikramaditya II, commissioned the Virupaksha and Mallikarjuna temples at Pattadakal.
tq: Start from the sure association between Vikramaditya II’s queens and the Pattadakal temples.
sec: Women in administration - queens and princesses as governors

s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes Akkadevi from Ayyana Mahadevi and Chamakamba?
o: Akkadevi was a Rashtrakuta feudatory, whereas the other two were Badami Chalukya queens.
Akkadevi governed Kisukad, whereas Ayyana Mahadevi and Chamakamba were temple builders rather than governors.
Akkadevi was an Eastern Chalukya queen, whereas the other two were Pallava governors.
Akkadevi built the Virupaksha temple, whereas the other two governed Kisukad.
x: Akkadevi, a Kalyani Chalukya princess, governed the province of Kisukad. The Eastern Chalukya queens Ayyana Mahadevi and Chamakamba are identified as temple builders, not governors.
tq: Compare the administrative role of Akkadevi with the temple-building role of the Eastern Chalukya queens.
sec: Women in administration - queens and princesses as governors

s:
Arrange the following Chalukya-Pallava conflicts in chronological order:
A. Vikramaditya II and Nandivarman II
B. Pulakesin II and Narasimhavarman I
C. Vikramaditya I and the Pallavas
D. Pulakesin II and Mahendravarman I
x: The four rounds occurred in the order: Pulakesin II–Mahendravarman I, Pulakesin II–Narasimhavarman I, Vikramaditya I–the Pallavas, and Vikramaditya II–Nandivarman II.
tq: Fix the first Pulakesin–Mahendravarman conflict and then place the later rulers sequentially.

s: Which of the following statements about the first two Chalukya-Pallava conflicts is correct?
o: Narasimhavarman I advanced to Kanchi in the first round, while Vikramaditya I was killed in the second round.
Mahendravarman I captured Vatapi in the first round, while Pulakesin II recovered it in the second round.
Nandivarman II defeated Pulakesin II in the first round, while Mahendravarman I captured Vatapi in the second round.
Pulakesin II advanced to Kanchi in the first round, while Narasimhavarman I defeated him in the second round.
x: In the first round Pulakesin II advanced to Kanchi and won territory in the Krishna-Godavari region. In the second round Narasimhavarman I defeated Pulakesin II and captured Vatapi.
tq: Contrast the result of the first round with the reversal in the second round.

s: The Pallava capture of Vatapi in 642 CE resulted in:
o: The replacement of the Chalukyas by the Rashtrakutas
x: Narasimhavarman I captured Vatapi in 642 CE, and Pulakesin II was killed in the conflict.
tq: Link the date, victor and consequence of the Vatapi campaign.

s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Vikramaditya II — Kanchi taken three times and spared
Nandivarman II — Overthrow of the Rashtrakutas
x: Nandivarman II was involved in the fourth Chalukya-Pallava conflict, in which Kanchi was taken and spared. The Rashtrakutas later replaced the Chalukyas and Dantidurga overthrew them.
tq: Find the swapped ruler–achievement pair.

s: The recovery of Vatapi around 655 CE is associated with:
x: Vikramaditya I recovered Vatapi around 655 CE after its occupation by the Pallavas.
tq: Use the approximate date to distinguish Vatapi’s recovery from its earlier capture.

s: For approximately how long did the Pallava occupation of Vatapi continue before Vikramaditya I recovered it?
x: The Pallava occupation of Vatapi lasted about 13 years until Vikramaditya I recovered it.
tq: Test the duration directly rather than confusing it with the broader period of rivalry.

s: The rivalry between the Chalukyas and Pallavas ended when:
o: The Cholas captured Vatapi in 642 CE
The Rashtrakutas replaced the Chalukyas in the mid-eighth century
The Hoysalas replaced both dynasties in the seventh century
x: The rivalry ended in the mid-eighth century when the Rashtrakutas replaced the Chalukyas.
tq: Identify the later political development rather than an event from the main war sequence.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the Battle of Pullalur is correct?
o: It was fought on the Narmada and was won by Harsha.
It was fought at Kanchi around 740 and was won by Vikramaditya II.
It was fought at Vatapi in 642 and was decisively won by Narasimhavarman I.
It was fought near Kanchi around 618–619 and its victor is disputed.
x: Pullalur, near Kanchi, was fought around 618–619. Pallava records credit Mahendravarman I, while Chalukya records claim victory for Pulakesin II, making the result disputed.
tq: Separate the disputed Pullalur result from the clearly recorded Vatapi victory.

s: The Battle of Manimangala, fought around 642 CE, was won by:
x: Narasimhavarman I defeated Pulakesin II at Manimangala around 642 CE. Pariyala and Suramara are also associated with this victory.
tq: Match the battle with its victor and approximate date.

s: Who was the Pallava general associated with the sack of Vatapi in 642 CE?
x: Paranjoti was the Pallava general associated with Narasimhavarman I’s sack of Vatapi.
tq: Distinguish a military commander from inscriptional authors and later feudatories.

s: Who assumed the title ‘Vatapikonda’?
x: Narasimhavarman I assumed the title Vatapikonda, meaning conqueror of Vatapi, after capturing the Chalukya capital.
tq: Use the title’s literal connection with the captured city.
sec: Titles won in these wars → ruler

s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Paramesvara — Pulakesin II
2. Vatapikonda — Narasimhavarman I
3. Kanchiyamkonda — Vikramaditya II
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
x: All three pairs are correct. Pulakesin II was styled Paramesvara, Narasimhavarman I was Vatapikonda, and Vikramaditya II was Kanchiyamkonda.
tq: Verify each title–ruler association before selecting the complete combination.
sec: Titles won in these wars → ruler

s: The title ‘Kanchiyamkonda’ is associated with the ruler who:
o: Took Kanchi during the reign of Nandivarman II
Recovered Vatapi from the Pallavas around 655 CE
x: Vikramaditya II assumed the title Kanchiyamkonda after taking Kanchi during the reign of Nandivarman II.
tq: Infer the ruler from the meaning of the title and the associated campaign.
sec: Titles won in these wars → ruler

s:
Which of the following statements about Vikramaditya II’s occupation of Kanchi is correct?
1. It occurred around 740 CE.
2. He entered Kanchi during the reign of Nandivarman II.
3. He plundered the Rajasimheshvara temple.
4. He left a Kannada inscription on a temple pillar.
x: Vikramaditya II entered Kanchi around 740 CE during Nandivarman II’s reign and left a Kannada inscription on a pillar. He gifted gold to the Rajasimheshvara temple rather than plundering it.
tq: Reject the negative action that reverses the ruler’s respectful treatment of Kanchi.
sec: Chalukya occupation of Kanchi - ruler, inscription

s: The Rajasimheshvara temple at Kanchi is also known as the:
x: The Rajasimheshvara temple is identified with the Kailasanatha temple at Kanchi.
tq: Distinguish the Kanchi temple from the similarly associated Pattadakal temples.
sec: Chalukya occupation of Kanchi - ruler, inscription

s: Which temple at Pattadakal commemorates Vikramaditya II’s victory at Kanchi and copies the Kailasanatha temple of Kanchi?
x: Lokamahadevi’s Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal commemorates Vikramaditya II’s victory and copies the Kailasanatha temple of Kanchi.
tq: Match the commemorative temple with the victory and its architectural model.
sec: Chalukya occupation of Kanchi - ruler, inscription

s: In the Chalukya administrative structure, the head of a Rashtra or Vishaya was known as:
x: Vishayapati was the official heading a Rashtra or Vishaya.
tq: Match the administrative unit with its specific officer.

s:
Which of the following statements regarding Chalukya revenue and urban centres is correct?
1. Land revenue was the main source of income.
2. Revenue could be collected in cash, kind and services.
3. Vatapi and Aihole were urban and trade centres.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct. Land revenue was the principal income and could be collected in cash, kind and services; Vatapi and Aihole functioned as urban and trade centres.
tq: Check whether the statements cover revenue, collection forms and urban functions without reversing them.

s: Agraharas under the Chalukyas were primarily:
o: Brahmin land grants managed by mahajanas
x: Agraharas were Brahmin land grants that spread widely, and mahajanas managed them. R.S. Sharma described this expansion as the proliferation of the feudal land grant system.
tq: Identify the institution by combining its land-grant character with its managing body.

s: R.S. Sharma described the widespread expansion of agraharas as the:
o: Expansion of the urban guild system
Proliferation of the feudal land grant system
x: R.S. Sharma termed the spread of agraharas the proliferation of the feudal land grant system.
tq: Recall the precise scholarly formulation rather than a broader description of administration.

s: Which of the following was NOT a feudatory of the Badami Chalukyas mentioned in this context?
x: The Alupas, Gangas and Sendrakas were feudatories. Dantidurga was the Rashtrakuta ruler who later overthrew the Chalukyas, not a Chalukya feudatory in this list.
tq: Separate the later conqueror from the feudatory groups.

s: Which statement correctly describes the political position of the Renati Chodas?
o: They were always independent rulers of Kanchi.
They were first feudatories of the early Pallavas and later of the Badami Chalukyas.
They replaced the Rashtrakutas in the mid-eighth century.
They governed Kisukad under the Kalyani Chalukyas.
x: In Rayalaseema, the Renati Chodas were initially feudatories of the early Pallavas and subsequently became feudatories of the Badami Chalukyas.
tq: Test the sequence of political allegiance rather than the geographical location alone.

s: Which of the following developments made Rayalaseema politically active during the Pallava-Chalukya wars?
o: The replacement of all local chiefs by the Cholas
The rise of the Renati Chodas, Banas and Vaidumbas
The migration of Harsha’s administration to the region
x: The wars stimulated political activity in Rayalaseema, including the rise of the Renati Chodas, Banas and Vaidumbas.
tq: Connect the regional consequence with the named local powers.

s: An eighth-century Telugu inscription in early Telugu script found at Pitikayagulla is significant because it indicates:
o: The origin of the Rashtrakuta dynasty in Kanchi
The direct rule of Harsha in Rayalaseema
x: The Pitikayagulla inscription indicates post-Badami Chalukya influence in Rayalaseema and is written in early Telugu script.
tq: Use the inscription’s place, date and script to identify its historical significance.

s: According to the reported ASI activity, how many inscriptions dating from the second to the sixteenth century were copied in the Nallamala Tiger Reserve?
x: The Archaeological Survey of India copied 25 inscriptions, dating from the second to the sixteenth century, in the Nallamala Tiger Reserve.
tq: Recall the exact numerical figure and chronological range together.

s: Which of the following correctly expresses the broader significance of the Chalukya-Pallava rivalry?
o: It ended with Harsha’s annexation of the Deccan.
It lasted only a few years and affected military history alone.
It was a century-long rivalry that shaped Deccan and Tamil politics and temple art.
It was confined to Rayalaseema and had no architectural consequences.
x: The rivalry lasted about a century and influenced Deccan and Tamil politics as well as temple art. The architectural relationship between Kailasanatha and Virupaksha illustrates this significance.
tq: Choose the option that combines the duration, geographical-political impact and artistic consequence.
